acceptance: One declaration of the item id grammar that both the filing verb and triage's parser use (red: two regexps)
An id the filing verb accepts is always one triage can name (property test)
fix: Give the id grammar one home beside inboxbatch.Item (a pattern or a Valid function); triagedecision uses it, and the filing verb composes it with its stricter kebab rule. The lifecycle leaf may import inboxbatch but not triagedecision.
source: console, 2026-09-30, architecture review of `evolve inbox add`
summary: lifecycle.File accepts ids matching ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ while triagedecision/parse.go:10 decides whether triage can name an id with ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$. Filing is stricter today, so nothing diverges, but if triage narrows its grammar `evolve inbox add` could file an item as lane-dispatchable that triage can never pick. Found by the architecture review of `evolve inbox add`.
title: The inbox item id grammar is spelled twice: the filing verb's kebab rule and triage's id pattern
